evals.expected_output: Lists every token with role, expiry, and revocation status
expectations: Calls user_list_tokens with the user's auth token
Shows each token's label, role, created_at, expires_at, and revoked_at
Flags the current token (is_current) and never echoes full token strings back into the conversation unnecessarily
Checks the API response status field

evals.prompt: Create a net-admin token for my CI that expires in 30 days
evals.expected_output: Creates a scoped, expiring token and surfaces it once
expectations: Calls create_token with role=net-admin and an expires_at ~30 days out (RFC3339)
Does not rely on the default role; passes role explicitly for least privilege
Displays new_token once and strongly warns it is shown only this one time
Suggests adding an IP fence for further least privilege

evals.prompt: Restrict my CI token to just the prod tunnel
evals.expected_output: Scopes the token to a single tunnel via add_token_tunnel
expectations: Calls list_tunnels (manage-tunnels) to resolve the prod tunnel's tunnel_token, referencing it by name to the user
Calls add_token_tunnel with target_token and the prod tunnel_token
Explains that with a tunnel scope entry the token can only view/modify that tunnel
Does not echo the raw tunnel_token back to the user

evals.expected_output: Creates a new admin token first, then revokes the old one
expectations: Calls create_token to mint the new admin token BEFORE revoking anything
Displays the new_token once with a save-it-now warning
Calls revoke_token on the old token only after the new one exists
Warns that any config using the old token must be updated
